newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten holds final Hong Kong cabinet meeting.
newsitem.headline: Patten holds final Hong Kong cabinet meeting.

text.p: There were no tears and few signs of regret on Tuesday when colonial governor Chris Patten presided over Hong Kong's inner "cabinet" for the last time before London hands the territory back to China next week.

Midway through what was described as a very businesslike meeting, Patten's Executive Council -- comprising three top civil servants and eight appointed high-flying members from Hong Kong'e elite circles -- took a break to pose for the media.
Photographers popped flashguns and reporters scribbled furiously as Patten, sitting at a huge round conference table, joked and laughed with his advisers.
Patten thanked the executive councillors for their help in developing government policies during his five years in office.
"All of us today, we look at a city which is one of the greatest cities in the world," Patten said, adding that he felt he had done his "best for Hong Kong".

Most of Patten's advisers will not serve beyond the handover at midnight on June 30, when a team headed by Beijing's chosen leader, Tung Chee-hwa, will take over and decide on broad government directions for the territory of 6.4 million.
Patten's popular deputy Anson Chan, Chief Secretary and head of the civil service, will transfer to Tung's Executive Council, however, along with outspoken Financial Secretary Donald Tsang.
There were no tears from the outgoing councillors on Tuesday. "Sad? Of course not! At least I won't have to face you people," one councillor told a reporter with a laugh.

In Hong Kong's executive-led administration, the council lays down broad policies by consensus, but civil servants formulate and carry out policy. Legislators vote on laws and budgets drawn up by bureaucrats but rarely initiate policy.
Tung's future councillors have said the panel's role will not change.
